Playbook.name: Windows — Offensive / Dual-Use Tooling Executed (Process Name — Covers Hosts Without Command-Line Auditing) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A known offensive/dual-use tool executed by process name (4688/Sysmon 1) - mimikatz, procdump, rubeus, sharphound/bloodhound, psexec, and similar. This name-based rule covers hosts lacking command-line auditing. Triage question: is this an attacker using a hacktool, or an authorised pentest/admin use of a dual-use tool?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: These tools perform credential theft, AD reconnaissance and lateral movement; execution outside an authorised engagement is a strong compromise signal.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the offensive-tool execution is an authorised engagement/admin use or malicious tradecraft.

Step.name: Tool, account, host and parent process
Step.Purpose: The tool, the running account, and the parent process establish intent and origin.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.name RLIKE "(?i)(mimikatz|mimilib|procdump|procdump64|rubeus|sharphound|bloodhound|psexec|psexec64|psexesvc|paexec|remcom|csexec|winexesvc|secretsdump|wce|gsecdump).*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.parent.name, user.name, process.command_line | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A credential tool (mimikatz/procdump/rubeus/secretsdump) is almost always malicious outside a pentest. Parent process (cmd/powershell/a dropper) and command_line (if present) show intent. Note the account - a service/normal user running mimikatz is compromise.

Step.name: Same tooling on other hosts / by the same account
Step.Purpose: The same offensive tool across hosts is an active campaign, not an isolated test.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND user.name == "$username" AND process.name RLIKE "(?i)(mimikatz|procdump|rubeus|sharphound|bloodhound|psexec|secretsdump|wce|gsecdump).*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS runs = COUNT(*), hosts = COUNT_DISTINCT(host.name), tools = VALUES(process.name) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Multiple hosts/tools by one account = campaign - escalate. A single run on one host by a pentester may be authorised.

Node.Condition: A credential-theft/AD-recon tool (mimikatz/procdump/rubeus/sharphound/secretsdump) run outside an authorised engagement, or the same tooling across hosts.
Execution during a documented, in-scope penetration test from the tester's host.
Dual-use tool (psexec) by an admin for a plausible task with no other indicators.
Node.Result: Benign Activity / Needs Escalation per role

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-OFFTOOL-DETAIL, INV-02-OFFTOOL-SPREAD to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Authorised penetration testing or a legitimate admin dual-use tool.

Indicators.Item: PsExec by a known admin for a known task.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the engagement/admin task; close as false_positive/benign_activity.
Isolate affected hosts; open IR; treat host credentials as exposed.
Hunt the tool's origin and other hosts; reset exposed credentials.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A security team's sanctioned tool run without prior notice.

Indicators.Item: No engagement record but confirmed benign.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm with the security team; document; require change records going forward.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
